network: The cert uplink carries TCP and no UDP. Its 100.100.100.100:53 is a raw TCP peer answering with dnsFake (wasi-dig's zone, real DNS wire messages); 100.64.9.9:53 refuses. Every UDP send fails with network unreachable, so the checklist covers the patched dighost.c's retry over TCP. No DoH in this build.
checklist: UDP network unreachable, at send (an uplink without UDP) or at setup (an address no uplink routes, #1370): dig prints ';; UDP network unreachable, retrying in TCP mode.' and asks over TCP well within one +time (SERVER … (TCP)), the TCP dial in the uplink log; +tcp prints no UDP line
full dig output: banner, ->>HEADER<<- NOERROR, flags qr rd ra, ANSWER section, SERVER line
dig +short for A, AAAA, MX, TXT (quoted, escaped), CNAME chain, NS, SOA, SRV, CAA, -x PTR, DNSKEY +nocrypto, HTTPS; +noall +answer; NXDOMAIN with the SOA in AUTHORITY
host: A, AAAA and MX by default, -t mx, reverse lookup, CNAME alias line, NXDOMAIN rc 1
nslookup: one-shot answer with Server/Address and Non-authoritative answer; -type=mx; an interactive session on stdin (server, set type=, queries, exit)
failures: refused server rc 9 (dig) / 1 (host); bad type is BIND's warning (rc 0); bad option rc 1

no server argument (9.20.29-2, homescoop#1282; slicc-kernel >= 1.137.0): /etc/resolv.conf is the kernel's (nameserver 127.0.0.53); host, dig +short and nslookup answer host.slicc.internal (10.0.2.2) and an uplink device name, laptop.slicc.internal (100.64.0.7), from the kernel's DNS stub, with nslookup's Server: 127.0.0.53; nobody.slicc.internal is NXDOMAIN; a public name (example.test A and MX) is forwarded to the uplink's nameserver 100.100.100.100 over TCP; with root's 'nameserver 100.100.100.100' in /etc/resolv.conf, host, dig and nslookup ask that instead (Server: 100.100.100.100)
users enforce: root, alice and bob get the same answers from dig and host; only root writes /etc/resolv.conf; alice can't write dig's output into bob's 0755 directory; bob's own output is his

+nssearch (9.20.29-2, homescoop#1379): dig +time=2 +tries=1 +nssearch @100.100.100.100 nss.test, whose NS is the resolver's own address, prints the server's SOA line ('SOA ns1.nss.test. hostmaster.nss.test. 2026102001 … from server 100.100.100.100 in N ms.') within 4 s and rc 0, with no 'timed out' or 'no servers could be reached'; +tcp +nssearch gives the same line; nss2.test with a refusing NS (100.64.9.9) first prints its 'Connection to 100.64.9.9#53(100.64.9.9) for nss2.test failed: connection refused.' and the other server's SOA, rc 0. 9.20.29-1: 'NS servers could not be reached', rc 9, with and without +tcp (NEGATIVE.md)
